story_type: first heavy rocket with strap-on solid boosters launches, boosters drop away on camera, historic film
hook: 2.5 million pounds of thrust and a 600 foot flame.
narration: Two and a half million pounds of thrust, and a trail of flame six hundred feet long.
This was the Air Force Titan Three C, launching from Cape Kennedy in 1965.
It strapped two huge solid fueled boosters to a liquid fueled core, a combination built to lift heavy loads into orbit.
The launch team ran the countdown from a control center inside the assembly building.
Twenty eight miles up, the spent solid motors were ejected and the liquid fueled core took over.
outcome: In its weightlifting test, the first Titan Three put twenty one thousand pounds of lead into orbit.
title: Titan III C and its giant boosters
question_comment: Would you rather watch this launch from the control room or the beach?

description:
The Air Force Titan III C, a liquid fueled core with two giant solid rocket boosters, launches from Cape Kennedy, Florida, in 1965, and its spent boosters are ejected 28 miles up.
